newsitem.title: CHILE: Coke to buy 24 mln shares in Chile bottler.
newsitem.headline: Coke to buy 24 mln shares in Chile bottler.

text.p: The Coca-Cola Company will buy 24 million new shares in Chilean bottler Embotelladora Andina which will be issued after shareholders approved a $250 million capital increase Monday, said an Andina official.
Coke, which announced its plans to invest in Andina several weeks ago, will buy the shares indirectly through a company known as Bottling Investment, said finance director Andres Olivos.
The Economy Ministry said in its monthly review of foreign investment that Bottling Investment has been authorized to buy seven percent of Andina.
Coke will invest some $140 million in the Chilean firm with the proceeds of the sale being used to finance Andina's plan to buy bottling and packaging companies in Argentina.
Andina will issue 43 million new shares in a private issue which will only be open to existing stockholders, said Olivos.
Inversiones Freire, which controls Andina, has agreed to waive its pre-emption rights and offer its new shares to Coca-Cola, he said.
Under the agreement with Coca-Cola, Andina will split its ordinary stock into A and B series with A shareholders controlling the board and B stockholders receiving an extra 10 percent dividend.
"This will give greater flexibility and allow Inversiones Freire to keep control on the company," Olivos told reporters after the shareholders meeting.
